- Prompt caching is a **hit rate**, not a memory size. Reused prefix → hit; changed prefix → miss. You cannot make the cached region larger than the prompt you send.
- On our two free-tier models, `cache_read` and `cache_write` pricing are both `None`, and `prompt_caching` is **not** in `supported_parameters`. So provider-side priced caching isn't in play at all.
- The `94% hit · 103k cached` figures in `/status` are OpenClaw's local prefix-reuse diagnostic, not evidence of a working provider cache tier. Read it as a diagnostic, not a knob.

- Two real levers to cut per-turn tokens: keep `/compact` occasional (each compaction rebuilds the prefix and *destroys* cache hits next turn), and never paste large files into chat (write to disk, summarise in chat — already AGENTS.md rule 2).
- Video: "Deepseek V4.1 Flash Runs With No GPU Just 64GB RAM" (channel: Kai / @kaiexplainsYT).
- Blocker: YouTube IP-blocked the host (timedtext 429, youtube_transcript_api `IpBlocked`, yt-dlp caption 429).
- Fix that worked: youtube_transcript_api through a free HTTP proxy from proxyscrape (1.20.101.19:8080) → full 27,022-char transcript to /tmp/wiMs92u-dk0.txt.
- Local summarizer at 127.0.0.1:5001 timed out at the 45s urllib limit (CPU-only DS-Coder-V2-Lite). Summarised in-context instead.
- Lesson: when captions 429/IpBlocked, try proxy path before declaring unavailable; and the 45s timeout in yt_transcript.py is too tight for CPU decode.
- Root cause: `timeout=45` urllib ceiling left over from the Qwen 3B llama-cli path. 5001 server (DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite, CPU-only) needs ~150s for a 4k-char prompt + 1200 tokens.

- Changes: `SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT=180` env-overridable; new `_local_summarize()` helper; rewrote `summarize_with_local_gpu` as two-stage (extract facts from 10k-char excerpt, then compress to structured summary) so it sees more of the video; error label no longer says "GPU".
- Verified: ran on wiMs92u-dk0, 168.9s, correct 284.33B / 155 GB / 76.87 GB / 8.66 tok/s / 82.7 Terminal Bench vs Opus 4.8's 85.0. Backup at /tmp/yt_transcript.py.bak.*
- Limitation found: 4k-char slice loses the back half — the 60.8% perplexity and Atomic Chat ladder didn't surface. Wants map-reduce or a chunk loop.
- Measured: 24 GB RAM total, 12.8 GB free, 4 GB swap, P2200 5 GB @6% util, Xeon E-2126G 6c, live deepseek-coder RSS 17.6 GB.
- Effective ceiling for a second model: ~11-12 GB weights + ~1 GB KV/overhead.
- Best candidate: Qwen3-30B-A3B (Apache-2.0, native 256k ctx). UD-IQ2_M 10.85 GB @32k = recommended start; UD-TQ1_0 8.09 GB fallback; UD-IQ3_XXS 12.91 GB too tight.
- gemma-4-31B dense = 31B active/token, ~3-5 tok/s on 6c, rejected. DeepSeek V3.x = 671B, impossible.
- This llama.cpp build (0.9.0-dev, b12283) shipped ONLY llama-server — no llama-cli/llama-quantize, so pre-quantised GGUFs only.
- P2200 cannot help: Pascal, no bf16, 5 GB < weights. Real lever = more RAM (16 GB DIMMs → 64-96 GB enables DS-V3.1-class 4-bit).
- Awaiting Bean's go to download + benchmark on a second port.
- 06:05 UTC: Daily digest posted — 2 sections with real links
- Control: 8k + --parallel 1 works, generates ~14 tok/s, survives.
- 16k default (CUDA0 KV offload) -> LOADS then DIES on first token. KV=4320 MiB (4096 CPU + 640 CUDA0) + 892 MiB compute buffer.
- 16k + `-nkvo` -> WORKS. KV stays in RAM, generates, survives. Free RAM after load ~6 GB.
- 24k + `-nkvo` -> short prompt works (14.3 tok/s), but a realistic 2k-token prompt killed it. Edge, not safe.
- 32k + `-nkvo` -> loads, DIES on first token. KV would be ~8.6 GB; too big for 24 GB box with 17.6 GB already used by 5001.
- Realistic 37.5k-char (~9.4k token) prompt at 16k: prefill slows 142->104->80->66->50 tok/s as cache fills, and the request blew past 240s. Prefill is the bottleneck, not VRAM.
- Verified live 5001 unaffected throughout; all probes killed, RAM back to ~13.1 GB used.
- CONCLUSION: 16k + -nkvo is the only safe upgrade on this box. 32k needs more RAM. q8_0 KV is not usable (FA disabled on Pascal P2200).

- Step 1 benchmark: GPU-resident KV (12k, --kv-offload) prefill 193 tok/s but decode 1.02 tok/s; -nkvo (32k) prefill 100 tok/s, decode 5.60 tok/s, 132.4s total. -ngl 99 impossible: 9,768 MiB on 5,120 MiB card. WINNER: -nkvo.
- Step 2 applied: deepseek-coder.service now `-c 32768 --parallel 1 --cont-batching -nkvo --spec-draft-ngl 99`. Live, n_ctx=32768.
- BORK: I first wrote `--nkvo` (invalid; correct is `-nkvo` / `--no-kv-offload`) -> auto-restart loop. Fixed. Backup: deepseek-coder.service.bak.1794640646
- Step 3: SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT 180->300, FETCH_EXCERPT_CHARS 10000->24000.

- REAL BUG FOUND: _local_summarize was one blocking call; 300s timeout threw away all generated text. Foreground repro: TimeoutError at exactly 300s while server still generating (task 10, 166 tok, 0.76 tok/s).
- FIX: rewrote _local_summarize to stream SSE (`"stream": True`), per-read timeout, keeps partial output as `[stream stopped: ...]`. Backup: /tmp/yt_transcript.py.bak.streaming

- Step 4 chunking: added CHUNK_CHARS=12000 and _split_chunks(); summarize_with_local_gpu now map-reduce (extract per chunk, tag PART i/N, merge, compress). Verified lossless: 27,022 chars -> [12000,12000,3022].

- KEY PERF FINDING: decode at high KV occupancy is ~0.7 tok/s vs ~14 tok/s cold-slot. A 24k-char excerpt with 900 max_tokens = ~20 min. Prefill is NOT the bottleneck (100-193 tok/s); DECODE is. My earlier "prefill is the ceiling" claim was wrong.
- STILL OPEN: single-pass vs chunked quality comparison. Single-pass run (task 182) in flight at 244 tok / 0.71 tok/s when session paused.
